reviews.text: I just watched Transformers for the first time, and I genuinely thought it was terrible. I know this movie has a massive fanbase and was hugely successful, but I honestly struggle to understand the appeal. For most of the runtime, it just felt like a constant barrage of explosions, screaming, fighting, cars, robots and things flying across the screen. Something is always happening, but somehow I still found it incredibly unengaging. The biggest problem for me was the plot. I know you’re supposed to just accept the concept of alien robots coming to Earth and disguising themselves as cars, but even within that setup, the story felt unnecessarily convoluted and ridiculous. Everyone is chasing the same objects, different groups keep appearing, robots are fighting robots, the military gets involved, and eventually it all just becomes noise. The dialogue also really didn’t work for me. So many lines felt unbelievably cheesy, to the point where I was genuinely uncomfortable at times. The humor, the dramatic speeches, the romantic scenes, the military dialogue – almost everything has this extremely specific mid-2000s blockbuster cheesiness to it. And I like Shia LaBeouf in plenty of other movies, but even he couldn’t really save this for me. There wasn’t a character, relationship or storyline that I felt particularly invested in. The one thing I can absolutely give the movie credit for is the visual effects. Especially considering this came out in 2007, the Transformers themselves still look impressive. The transformations are incredibly detailed, the CGI interacts convincingly with the real environments, and I can imagine that seeing this on a huge cinema screen at the time probably felt pretty revolutionary. But great effects aren’t enough for me when I don’t care about anything that’s happening around them. It also feels incredibly representative of a certain kind of American blockbuster from that era: huge cars, military hardware, attractive people, explosions, loud music and everything constantly turned up to eleven. I can see how that spectacle appealed to a massive audience, especially in 2007, but it really isn’t for me. By the end I genuinely felt exhausted rather than entertained. There’s very little here that made me think about the movie afterwards beyond wondering how something this loud could somehow still bore me. I’m definitely not a Transformers fan, and this movie certainly didn’t turn me into one. The effects are impressive, but almost everything else – the dialogue, the characters, the plot and the nonstop action – did absolutely nothing for me. I will not be watching this again.

2.5/10 "The first Transformers is actually kinda good." That's a sentence I've heard loads of times. I have no idea what's going on in the minds of the people who say that. The first Transformers is one of the most embarrassing AAA productions I know of. And it only goes downhill from here. The entire movie's attitude is just loathsome. It tries to mash a few dark and serious elements together with dialogue and comic relief straight out of a frat house. Every character is unbelievably obnoxious. I don't understand why anyone would ever want to follow these people, or why anyone would ever care about anything that's happening. The entire world this film takes place in is insufferable, and the whole thing feels like it was made by a bunch of college jocks. Everything about it is just annoying. It's also weird how often the movie seems to be attempting some kind of parody of the American government. The directing is actually okay for a production like this. The blend of on-set footage and CGI works great, and Bay directs the actors competently. What I do find hilarious, however, is just how clearly his background in music video directing shines through in quite a few shots. That - and especially how aggressively everything is geared towards being cool and badass - comes off as incredibly cringe and try-hard. Ninety per cent of the story is made up of some lame McGuffin fetch quest with stakes I couldn't care less about, because the world and the characters suck. And it all eventually culminates in one of the least exciting third acts I've ever seen. There's battle scene after battle scene, but not only do I barely know what's going on because half the Transformers look the same, I also don't really care. It's just more and more fighting, and I realised that watching Transformers transform into and out of cars had already gotten boring the third time around. This film is filled to the brim with stupid shit and is, in general, one of the most unenjoyable ways to spend two hours and fifteen minutes that I can think of.

Some say that he makes good first entries and that he always finds a place for spectacle. All I know is that this movie sucks. While the story between Sam (Shia LaBeouf) and Bumblebee (Mark Ryan) can be a grounding moment, it isn’t enough force to get it on land. Neither is Peter Cullen’s performance as Optimus Prime, the score, or the fights. Optimus owing his life to Sam does make sense though and Optimus says his iconic lines and good new lines. But that’s just about where the fun ends. First, Michael Bay doesn’t seem to respect the lore for Cybertron is supposed to be habitable, at least for the Decepticons. There’s too many subplots, the wrong tone with the military and disaster film aspects, too detailed CGI with the Decepticons being all gray, too much human stuff, bad jokes, especially Bumblebee and the lubricant and Ratchet (Robert Foxworth) saying Sam’s pheromone levels suggests he wants to have a kid with Mikaela (Megan Fox). Also the whole Sam selling his great-grandfather’s glasses on eBay is meaningless. Shia LaBeouf is just alright as Sam, he tries, but Bay, Roberto Orci, and Alex Kurtzman don’t give him much to work with. So little that Sam doesn’t feel like a hero as he’s given no space to grow into one. Megan Fox is also not impressive as she is subjected to Bay sexualizing her, even when doing something as simple as looking into what’s wrong with a car. Although that’s more so how she is dressed. Bay and Fox have history, as she was portrayed at 15 quite suggestively in Bad Boys II (2003), and Fox did not forget that. This movie doesn’t feel like a step in the right direction with Fox in Bay’s movies. Especially since she doesn’t have much of a character and is mostly here so Bay can feature the male gaze. Dwelling on humans unfortunately means Optimus and Megatron (Hugo Weaving) don’t appear until an hour in, and Megatron is not an active threat until the movie is nearly over. Speaking of Megatron, Weaving is nothing impressive. If they brought back Frank Welker, who voiced Megatron in G1 to pair with Cullen’s Optimus, it may have been more believable that these two had history. Weaving can act, he was good as Red Skull, but he can’t really in this movie. Speaking of the actual Transformers, Bumblebee having no lines gives him no character and we also don’t see him take the form of the 2007 Camaro. Jazz dying without any investment in his character is straight up shrewd. So now I’ve gotten past the problems with the characters. Does that mean the story’s good? I wish the answer was “Yes”. First, revisionist history opens a flood of confusion. The Hoover Dam was built due to the Cube (and the AllSpark) being there? And the two worlds have met before? So why then do the humans pretend they don’t know what’s happening? If none of the revisionist history was here and the events of the movie were the first time Cybertron’s inhabitants met humans on Earth, it would be a much cleaner story. Second, it takes too long to get to what really matters. It takes like 45 minutes to an hour to get to what matters, the Decepticons want the Cube and the Autobots can’t let that happen. Because of the human stuff, it prevents us from just cutting to the chase. Overall, a first entry that could have been worse, but does not provide encouragement for what’s next. 3/10 or 1½ stars.

“Transformer” I know these movies are really popular from my generation but I’ve actually never watched any of the Michael Bay Transformers movies before in my life. Nor do I really care about this franchise. I haven’t even watched any Transformers cartoons when I was a kid. I owned no Transformers toys aside from some  Happy Meal toys. So I know virtually nothing about this series. Anyway watching this movie, it probably was a lot like the Michael Bay Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles movies I don’t know anything about Transformers so I can’t confidently say that but that’s definitely the vibe I got with this movie. The movie is actually pretty fun whenever the Transformers were on the screen, however that barely happened most of the movies does Shia LaBeouf and Megan Fox dicking around. Just like how most of Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (2014) was just Megan Fox trying to get a news story and barely had the title characters in the movie. Same thing here I think it takes like over 50 minutes before we even see a transformer on screen. The movie was actually fun whenever we got to see them transforms especially when they’re in fights but whenever it’s Shia LaBeouf bitching about high school it got pretty annoying and pretty boring. This movie should be nonstop Transformers action but now we had to squeeze in Shia LaBeouf and Megan Fox in here. I mean at least I like that shot of Megan Fox over the hood of the car I think we’re gonna agree that shot define a generation of boys. Yeah I was not really much as the rest of the movie is pretty boring. If there’s not a transformer on the screen the movie is painfully boring, even the human action stuff like whenever we see the military guys go to war even that stuff pretty boring uninteresting. I like the one guy who was wearing a Redskins jersey for the entire movie, not cause I liked his character or found him interesting or anything. I just like seeing Redskins merch in media cause it’s a reminder that no matter how hard the NFL tries they’re not gonna erase the Redskins from history. But not much to say this is barely a Transformers movie. I wasn’t watching the sequel but no for when I heard this is the best one out of all five. Maybe I’ll check out “Rise Of The Beast”
